tasks.short: Review the order and last session note, perform bronchopulmonary drainage, instruct breathing exercises, and write the session note.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist reviews the order and the last session note
Respiratory therapist performs bronchopulmonary drainage with positioning and percussion
Respiratory therapist instructs patients in performance of breathing exercises
Respiratory therapist reads oxygen saturation and respiratory rate from the bedside monitor and types them into the session note
Respiratory therapist writes the session note with sputum, tolerance and advice

tasks.design: The ward view in the electronic health record ({OTHER}) shows the therapy order with the last session note on one screen. On wards where bedside monitors are connected to the record, oxygen saturation and respiratory rate arrive through the hospital's device interface and the therapist confirms them; elsewhere they are typed. The session note has fixed fields for sputum and tolerance. Drainage and teaching breathing exercises stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders and notes were found on separate screens and monitor values typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Bedside monitors send vital signs to the health record.
tasks.still_hard: Sputum and how the patient tolerated the session are judged, not measured.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling through the hands when secretions start to move.

reach.learn: Whether structured notes help between sessions.

evidence.claim: Bedside monitors can send vital signs into the electronic health record.
The medical dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the therapy order to the session note; changing the order is outside.

Input contract for s4: vital signs written to the record by the bedside monitor through the hospital's device interface, run by clinical IT, on connected wards; the therapist confirms each value; fallback is typing.
Coverage: about 60% of the therapist's patients lie on wards with connected monitors; s4 is priced at that share.
Drainage and instruction do not change; patients' time does not change.

already_counted.description: Respiratory therapist confirms imported monitor values.

incremental.description: Clinical IT keeps the monitor-to-record mapping working after device or record updates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: wards whose monitors do not link to the record; high: all monitors linked.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the demonstration and equipment, demonstrate respiratory care procedures to trainees, watch them practise and correct them, and sign off competences.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist prepares the demonstration and equipment
Respiratory therapist demonstrates respiratory care procedures to trainees and other healthcare personnel
Respiratory therapist watches trainees practise and corrects them
Respiratory therapist signs off trainees' competences on paper forms

tasks.design: Procedure cards and short videos per respiratory procedure sit in the hospital's learning system ({LMS}), so trainees prepare before the demonstration and less setup explanation is needed. Competences are signed off in the same system instead of on paper. Demonstrating and correcting stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each demonstration was prepared from scratch and competences signed on paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems hold procedure cards, videos and competence sign-off.
tasks.still_hard: Hands-on skill is learned at the bedside, not from a video.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a trainee's hesitation before a suction catheter goes in.

reach.learn: Whether digital sign-off shows gaps sooner.

evidence.claim: Hospital learning systems hold procedure cards, videos and competence sign-off.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training plan to competence records; formal exams are outside.
Input contract: training plans from the clinical educator; fallback is paper forms.
Demonstrating and correcting do not change.
Trainees' preparation time is about the same.

incremental.description: Respiratory therapist updates procedure cards when practice changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: procedures without cards yet; high: all common procedures carded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain the condition to patient and family, teach inhaler, breathing and equipment techniques, choose leaflets, send them to the portal, and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist explains the condition to the patient and family
Respiratory therapist teaches disease management techniques such as breathing exercises, inhaler use and equipment care
Respiratory therapist selects and prints leaflets for the patient
Respiratory therapist hands the leaflets to the patient
Patient phones the therapist with follow-up questions
Respiratory therapist answers patients' follow-up questions by phone

tasks.design: Vetted, guideline-based patient information and the hospital's own leaflets are linked to diagnoses in the health record ({OTHER}). The therapist ticks what fits, and after that check the patient portal sends it, with videos of inhaler technique. Portal pages built from the same vetted texts answer common follow-up questions, so fewer calls reach the therapist. Explaining and teaching stay with the therapist; no chatbot gives personal advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were printed one by one and every question came by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals send chosen information and host vetted pages.
tasks.still_hard: Patients with low literacy or no portal access need paper and calls.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a patient's real problem with the inhaler is fear, not technique.

reach.learn: Whether portal pages cut repeat calls.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts offers guideline-based patient information written by the NHG, FMS and the Patiëntenfederatie.
Health data are special category data; solely automated care decisions need an Article 22(2) basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the diagnosis to answered questions; medication changes are outside.
Input contract: leaflets approved by the pulmonology department; vetted public patient information; fallback is printed leaflets.
Patients read portal pages before phoning; the reading is priced as customer time.
Explaining and teaching do not change.

incremental.description: Respiratory therapist reports outdated leaflets to the department.
Patients read portal pages first; some questions end there.

approvals.approved_version: The information as chosen by the therapist in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older patients without portal access; high: most patients use the portal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign patients and tasks to technicians and students, supervise their care at the bedside, teach during care, co-sign their notes, and complete students' evaluation forms.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist lists the respiratory patients and their orders for the shift
Respiratory therapist assigns patients and tasks to technicians and students at the start of the shift
Respiratory therapist supervises the care given by students, respiratory therapy technicians and assistants at the bedside
Respiratory therapist teaches students during patient care
Respiratory therapist checks and co-signs notes written by students and technicians
Respiratory therapist fills in students' evaluation forms

tasks.design: A shift board in the health record ({OTHER}) lists respiratory patients with their orders and lets the therapist assign each one to a technician or student. Notes awaiting co-signature sit in one queue with the changes highlighted. Student evaluation forms are filled in the school's online form. Supervising and teaching at the bedside stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments were written on a whiteboard and notes found one by one for co-signing.
tasks.enabler_now: Health records offer shift boards and co-signature queues.
tasks.still_hard: Busy shifts leave little time for teaching whatever the tools.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when to let a student struggle and when to step in.

reach.learn: Whether the shift board cuts handover questions.

evidence.claim: Health records offer shift boards and queues for notes awaiting co-signature.
The medical dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient list to student evaluations; formal grading by the school is outside.
Input contract: patient lists and orders from the record; evaluation forms from the training school; fallback is the whiteboard.
Supervising and teaching do not change.
Co-sign data are not used to rate staff.

incremental.description: Respiratory therapist updates assignments when patients move.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: units with few students and technicians; high: teaching units with many students.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The respiratory therapist keeps treatment, teaching patients and supervising at the bedside; typing values, paper sign-offs, printing and repeat calls shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using shift boards and portal pages
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who spends saved minutes at the bedside.
